claim_reviews.conclusion: The relation different-common-word is too categorical. The varieties show a useful lexical preference—Indonesian barang bekas versus Malaysian barang/barangan terpakai—but the Malaysian phrase barang terpakai is an accepted equivalent and forms overlap in cross-variety exposure. The relation should be qualified as a preference with overlap, if that relation is available.
claim_reviews.evidence_limitation: The reviewed sources establish acceptance and meaning, but do not provide directly comparable national frequency data.

claim_reviews.conclusion: Missing. A learner-facing contrast should note that Malay bekas commonly means a former person/status, a trace, or a container, while terpakai is the direct standard choice for second-hand goods; Indonesian barang bekas is therefore not a safe one-to-one Malaysian transfer.
claim_reviews.subject: False-friend contrast

rationale: The English sense and both proposed forms are understandable and accepted, but the national split is materially overstated as an unqualified different-common-word relation. Malaysian authoritative sources explicitly use barang terpakai and barangan terpakai for second-hand goods, while Indonesian barang bekas is the ordinary form. The card also lacks a useful false-friend contrast for bekas, whose Malay meanings commonly include former, trace, or container. Frequency comparison across national varieties is limited.
